query: What learner needs and pain points appear in survey responses?

per_column.name: instructional_format
per_column.rationale: The mode of instruction (live, async, project-based) is a contextual attribute of the learning environment that may CAUSE or predict needs/pain points, but it is not itself an aspect OF a learner's needs or pain. It classifies the delivery format, not a facet of the concept.

per_column.name: teacher_responsiveness
per_column.rationale: Support/responsiveness from teachers is a genuine dimension of learner needs and a recognized pain point (absent_or_unresponsive). It captures the 'support/instructor availability' aspect of the concept.

per_column.name: engagement_level
per_column.rationale: Disengagement/withdrawal is a core experiential pain point for learners; engagement is a constitutive aspect of learner experience and unmet needs (motivation/attention).

per_column.name: peer_interaction_loss
per_column.rationale: Loss of peer interaction/community is a direct, named pain point and reflects the social/relational facet of learner needs.

per_column.name: handson_gap_type
per_column.rationale: Gaps in hands-on/experiential learning (labs, studios, manipulatives) are concrete unmet needs; this is a legitimate practical/experiential facet of the concept.

per_column.name: positive_adaptation
per_column.rationale: Positive adaptations (innovative curriculum, learner growth, community building) are successes/bright spots, the OPPOSITE of needs and pain points. They are not a part-of the pain-point concept and shift the axis away from it.

judge.rationale: Four of six columns are true facets of learner needs/pain points, carving into support, engagement, social/peer, and hands-on/experiential aspects. These are fairly non-overlapping, though engagement and peer_interaction_loss have some conceptual bleed (disengagement often driven by social loss), modestly lowering exclusivity. instructional_format is an external context predictor and positive_adaptation is the opposite polarity (successes, not pains), so both fail the part-of test. Coverage of the pain-point concept is partial: important facets like technology/access barriers, cognitive/academic difficulty, workload/time management, and assessment/feedback needs are missing, keeping exhaustiveness moderate.
